title: Week 22 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “elasticity”?
options: Ability to produce more output with the same resources.
A tax whose burden consumes a larger share of lower income than higher income.
Conduct attributable to government and therefore subject to many constitutional limits.
A measure of how responsive one variable is to a change in another.
questions.explanation: Elasticity means a measure of how responsive one variable is to a change in another.
choices: Ability to produce more output with the same resources.
A tax whose burden consumes a larger share of lower income than higher income.
Conduct attributable to government and therefore subject to many constitutional limits.
A measure of how responsive one variable is to a change in another.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “price elasticity of demand”?
options: A reasonable basis, grounded in facts, to believe a crime occurred or evidence will be found.
A person who benefits from a good or action without contributing to its cost.
A system combining markets with public regulation, provision, taxation, and social insurance.
Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price.
questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand means responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “consumer surplus”?
options: Selecting and emphasizing aspects of an issue to shape interpretation.
A structured set of beliefs about government, society, rights, economy, and public priorities.
Law developed through judicial decisions, custom, and precedent.
The difference between willingness to pay and the price actually paid.
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus means the difference between willingness to pay and the price actually paid.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “producer surplus”?
options: Conduct attributable to government and therefore subject to many constitutional limits.
The difference between the market price and the minimum a producer would accept.
A supporter of ratifying the Constitution and strengthening national government.
A judicial opinion disagreeing with the majority’s result or reasoning.
questions.explanation: Producer surplus means the difference between the market price and the minimum a producer would accept.
choices: Conduct attributable to government and therefore subject to many constitutional limits.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “tax incidence”?
options: A presidential directive governing executive-branch operations within claimed legal authority.
The distribution of a tax’s economic burden between buyers and sellers.
A person, group, institution, or community affected by or able to influence a decision.
Interest and principal payments associated with public debt.
questions.explanation: Tax incidence means the distribution of a tax’s economic burden between buyers and sellers.
choices: A presidential directive governing executive-branch operations within claimed legal authority.
The distribution of a tax’s economic burden between buyers and sellers.
A person, group, institution, or community affected by or able to influence a decision.
Interest and principal payments associated with public debt.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “deadweight loss”?
options: Powers exercised by both national and state governments.
Gains from exchange lost when policy or distortion prevents mutually beneficial transactions.
Revenue minus explicit and implicit costs.
A price and quantity at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 22 inquiry?
options: A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student identifies which side is less elastic before predicting tax incidence and distinguishes statutory remittance from economic burden.
